title: Delivery of Therapeutic siRNA to the CNS Using Cationic and Anionic Liposomes
protocol: Use a 1:1 DOTAP (1,2-dioleoyl-3-trimethylammonium-propane):cholesterol ratio for LSPCs.
Mix 2 nmoles of DOTAP and 2 nmoles of cholesterol into 10 ml of a 1:1 chloroform:methanol solution in a flask.
Evaporate 9 ml of the chloroform:methanol solution using N2 gas in a fume hood.
Evaporate the last 1 ml of solvent in a fume hood overnight without gas.
Pour heated 10 ml of a 10% sucrose solution onto the thin lipid film slowly at 1 ml/min while gently swirling the flask.
Maintain the 10% sucrose and flask with lipids at 55 °C so that the lipid molecules remain in the gel-liquid phase.
Allow lipids to rehydrate at 55 °C for at least one hour before sizing the liposomes.
Add 1 ml of the heated liposome suspension to one of the syringes on the extruder.
Pass the suspension between the two syringes 11 times.
Ensure that the suspension is in the opposite syringe than the starting syringe after 11 passes.
Size the liposomes through a 0.45 µm filter.
Size the liposomes through a 0.2 µm filter to generate large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs).
Incubate 20 μl of the 4 nmole liposome suspension with 200 μl of a 20 μM stock siRNA solution for 10 min at room temperature.
Incubate 80 μl of a 500 µM RVG-9r solution with the siRNA/liposome solution for 10 min at room temperature.
Store LSPCs at 4 °C for several hours after preparation if not used immediately.
Mix 2.2 nmoles of either DSPE or DOTAP, 1.6 nmoles of cholesterol, and 0.2 nmoles of DSPE-PEG into 10 ml of a 2:1 chloroform:methanol solution in a flask for PALETS preparation.
Rehydrate the liposomes in 10 ml of 1x PBS heated to 75 °C at 1 ml/min.
Allow lipids to rehydrate at 75 °C for at least 1 hour before sizing.
Size the liposome suspension through a 0.45 µm filter.
Size the liposome suspension through a 0.2 µm filter to generate large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs).
Pipette 20 µl of each of the 4 nmole (200 µM) liposome suspensions into single use aliquots.
Lyophilize the liposomes for 30 min using a benchtop freeze dryer.
Incubate 200 µl of a 20 µM (4 nmole total) stock siRNA solution with 1.4 µl of a 26.6 µM protamine sulfate solution for 10 min at RT.
Rehydrate the DOTAP PALETS liposomes with 200 µl of a 4 nmole stock solution of siRNA.
Rehydrate DSPE PALETS liposomes with 201.4 µl of the siRNA/protamine solution.
Incubate the liposome/siRNA solution for 10 min at RT.
Add 10 µl of a 60 mM EDC solution to the liposome/siRNA solution for both DOTAP and DSPE PALETS.
Add 10 µl of a 150 mM sulfo-NHS solution to the liposome/siRNA solution for both DOTAP and DSPE PALETS.
Incubate the EDC and sulfo-NHS with the siRNA/liposome suspension for 2 hr at RT.
Incubate 80 µl of a 500 µM (40 nmole total) stock RVG-9r solution with the siRNA/liposome crosslinking solution for 10 min at RT.
Measure the concentration of siRNA before and after the addition of protamine and liposomes using a spectrophotometer set at 260 nm.
Filter the unencapsulated siRNA from the liposome/encapsulated siRNA suspension using 50 kDa centrifugal filters.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 20 min.
Measure the concentration of unencapsulated siRNA in the filtrate and the concentration of encapsulated siRNA in the retentate using a spectrophotometer at 260 nm.
Expose mice to a heat lamp for 5-10 minutes to dilate vasculature.
Anesthetize mouse with 2-3% isofluorane/oxygen flow 5-10 minutes before injection and during the injection process.
Confirm anesthetization when animal is no longer ambulant and respirations have slowed by performing a toe pinch test.
Place the mouse on its back or side to access the tail vein.
Apply vet ointment on mouse's eyes to prevent drying while under anesthesia.
Wipe/spray the tail with 70% EtOH.
Inject 300 µl of LSPCs or PALETS onto the tail vein using a 26 G insulin syringe, starting distally and moving proximally if necessary.
Place mouse in a clean cage until it maintains sternal recumbency.
Monitor closely to safeguard against overheating; place mouse on a heating pad or under a heat lamp if recovery takes longer than 5-15 minutes.
Monitor the animal several hours after injection to ensure anesthesia wears off, and there are no ill effects of the treatment.
Allow the LSPCs or PALETS to circulate for at least 24 hr.
Euthanize mice with a 20% CO2 flow rate for 15 min.
Cut away the skin and skull of the mouse using scissors.
Peel away half a hemisphere of brain from the skull using tongs or the end of a pair of scissors.
Press half a hemisphere of brain through a 40 µm mesh cell strainer using 2.5 ml of FACS buffer in a Petri dish with the plunger of a syringe.
Rinse the cell strainer and Petri dish with an additional 2.5 ml of FACS buffer.
Transfer the single cell suspension to a 15 ml conical tube on ice.
Centrifuge 100 µl of the 5 ml single cell suspension in a microcentrifuge tube for 5 min at 350 x g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of FACS buffer.
Spin the cells again for 5 min at 350 x g.
Repeat with another 1 ml of FACS buffer.
Incubate the cells in 100 µl of a 1:100 dilution of a 0.5 mg/ml rat anti-mouse Fc block in FACS buffer for 30-60 min on ice.
Pellet and wash the cells as previously described.
Keep the cell suspension on ice during all steps.
Incubate the cells in 100 µl of a 20 µg/ml fluorescent antibody against mouse PrPC in 7% mouse serum in FACS buffer on ice for 30-60 min.
Pellet and wash the cells as in step 4.5.
Keep the cell suspension on ice.
Pellet and re-suspend the cells in 1 ml of RBC lysis buffer (1x PBS, 155 mM NH4Cl, 12 mM NaHCO3, 0.1 mM EDTA) for 1 min.
Pellet as in step 4.5.
Resuspend the cells in 1 ml of FACS buffer.
Keep the cell suspension on ice.
Analyze PrPC expression using a flow cytometer as described previously.
Gate live cells from total cell population.
Gate PrPC+ cells from live cell population to determine MFI (median fluorescent intensity).
